title_en: Yu Cunku v. Dong Chengbin and Dong Chengzhen — dispute over house sale
keywords_en: Civil; dispute over a house sale contract; first-instance trial; basic people's court; Sichuan Province; natural person; General Principles of the Civil Law; Urban Real Estate Administration Law; validity of house sale agreement; transfer of allocated land use rights; obligation to register property right change; partial support; house sale; allocated land; property registration not completed; good faith; land use rights; Dong Chengzhen house sale dispute
full_text_en:
Yu Cunku v. Dong Chengbin and Dong Chengzhen — Dispute over House Sale

Plaintiff (Counterclaim Defendant): Yu Cunku, male, 67 years old, retired employee, residing at Shangdong Street, Luocheng Town, Guanghan City, Sichuan Province.

Agent ad litem: Ran Qifa, lawyer of Luopeng Law Firm, Deyang City, Sichuan Province.

Defendant (Counterclaim Plaintiff): Dong Chengbin, male, 35 years old, unemployed, residing at Guihua Street, Luocheng Town, Guanghan City, Sichuan Province.

Defendant (Counterclaim Plaintiff): Dong Chengzhen, female, 42 years old, worker, residing at Dongcheng Street, Bazhong City, Sichuan Province.

Agent ad litem: Yang Jun, legal worker of Guanghan City Legal Affairs Office, Sichuan Province.

Plaintiff Yu Cunku filed an action with the Guanghan City People's Court of Sichuan Province against defendants Dong Chengbin and Dong Chengzhen over a dispute concerning a house sale, and Dong Chengbin and Dong Chengzhen simultaneously filed a counterclaim.

Plaintiff Yu Cunku alleged: In accordance with the house sale agreement signed with the two defendants, after receiving the purchase price paid by the two defendants and after the two defendants took possession of the house, the plaintiff repeatedly sought out the two defendants as agreed but could not locate them, with the result that the registration of the transfer of ownership of the house has still not been completed to date. Since the land on which the house is situated is allocated land, which cannot be transferred according to law, and the ownership of the house has not yet been changed, the plaintiff requests that the house sale agreement between the plaintiff and the defendants be confirmed as invalid, that the two defendants be ordered to return the house to the plaintiff and the rent of RMB 33,000 collected during their occupation of the house, and that the costs of this action be borne by the defendants.

The two defendants answered and counterclaimed: The defendants have performed their obligation to pay the purchase price in accordance with the house sale agreement signed with the plaintiff. Subsequently, because the plaintiff moved without notifying the defendants, contact with the plaintiff was lost, and the registration procedures for the change of ownership of the house and the land use right have still not been completed to date. The plaintiff's breach of contract has infringed the lawful rights and interests of the two defendants. The reasons asserted by the plaintiff for the invalidity of the house sale agreement are untenable, and the agreement should continue to be performed. The counterclaim requests that the plaintiff be ordered to pay liquidated damages of RMB 5,000 to the two defendants, compensate the two defendants for their other losses, and assume the obligation to complete the registration of the change of the land use right for the land occupied by the house. According to the agreement, the land use right assignment fee should be paid by the plaintiff.

The Guanghan City People's Court of Sichuan Province found the following facts upon trial:

On December 11, 1997, the plaintiff Yu Cunku and the defendants Dong Chengbin and Dong Chengzhen signed a house sale agreement, stipulating: A shop premises located on the ground floor, Axes 10-11, Building 103, Guihua Street, Luocheng Town, Guanghan City, is the private property of Yu Cunku and is currently leased by Yang Jun; after obtaining Yang Jun's consent, Yu Cunku now sells this property to Dong Chengbin and Dong Chengzhen at a price of RMB 122,000; the land use right assignment fee arising from the house sale shall be borne by Yu Cunku; taxes and transfer fees shall be borne by Dong Chengbin and Dong Chengzhen; notarization fees shall be shared equally by both parties; after the house is sold, the original lease agreement shall remain in effect; the parties shall abide by the agreement, and if either party breaches the agreement, it shall pay the other party liquidated damages of RMB 5,000.

On December 11, the parties completed the notarization procedures for the house sale agreement. On the same day, the defendants Dong Chengbin and Dong Chengzhen paid the plaintiff Yu Cunku cash of RMB 122,000, and Yu Cunku issued a receipt and delivered the house to Dong Chengbin and Dong Chengzhen. Dong Chengbin and Dong Chengzhen, as lessors, have continued to lease the house to date.

The house in question was a commercial apartment purchased by the plaintiff Yu Cunku from Guanghan Construction Development Corporation in September 1993. The land occupied by the house was obtained through allocation. The Guanghan City land administration department confirmed that the Guanghan City People's Government permits the transfer of real estate on such land after the completion of land use right assignment procedures. At the time Yu Cunku and the defendants Dong Chengbin and Dong Chengzhen completed the notarization of the house sale agreement, Yu Cunku had not yet obtained the land use right certificate for the land occupied by the house. Ten days after the notarization procedures, Yu Cunku obtained a certificate of allocated land use right in his own name for an area of 8.30 square meters. Because both parties moved after signing the house sale agreement and failed to notify each other, resulting in loss of contact, the registration procedures for the change of ownership of the house and the land use right have not been completed as agreed. On March 2, 1999, when Dong Chengbin and Dong Chengzhen unilaterally applied to the house administration department for the registration of the change of house ownership, it was not completed due to obstruction by Yu Cunku.

The above facts are confirmed by documentary evidence including the house sale agreement, notarial certificate, cash receipt, and certificate of allocated land use right, as well as witness testimony and statements of the parties.

The Guanghan City People's Court of Sichuan Province held:

Article 55 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "A civil juristic act shall satisfy the following conditions: (1) the actor has the corresponding capacity for civil conduct; (2) the expression of intention is genuine; (3) it does not violate the law or social public interests." Article 57 provides: "A civil juristic act shall be legally binding from the time of its establishment. An actor may not alter or rescind the act without legal provisions or the consent of the other party." The shop premises located on the ground floor, Axes 10-11, Building 103, Guihua Street, Luocheng Town, Guanghan City, is the private property of the plaintiff Yu Cunku. Although the land occupied by the house was obtained through allocation, the local people's government with approval authority permits the transfer of real estate on such land after the completion of land use right assignment procedures. When Yu Cunku signed the agreement to transfer the house with the defendants Dong Chengbin and Dong Chengzhen, both parties had the corresponding capacity for civil conduct, their expressions of intention were genuine, the content of the agreement was the sale of private property that was legally permissible to sell, and a provision was made regarding the handling of land assignment procedures, without harming national or social public interests. Therefore, the agreement signed by the parties was legally established and is legally binding on both parties, and neither party may unilaterally rescind the agreement without the consent of the other.

Article 59 of the Urban Real Estate Administration Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "The State implements a system of registration and certification of land use rights and house ownership." Article 60, paragraph 3, provides: "When real estate is transferred or changed, an application for registration of the change of real estate shall be submitted to the real estate administration department of the local people's government at or above the county level, and an application for registration of the change of land use right shall be submitted to the land administration department of the same level people's government on the basis of the changed house ownership certificate. After verification by the land administration department of the same level people's government, the people's government of the same level shall replace or amend the land use right certificate." Although the house sale agreement signed by the plaintiff Yu Cunku and the defendants Dong Chengbin and Dong Chengzhen was legally established, it does not have the effect of transferring the ownership of the house to which the agreement refers until the procedures required by the above provisions are completed. The parties shall perform their respective obligations to complete the procedures for the change of ownership in accordance with the provisions of law and the agreement.

It should be pointed out that the statement "the transfer of a house is valid only if registration of the change is made" means that although an intention to buy and sell real estate can be established through the signing of an agreement, if it is not registered, the effect of transferring ownership of the real estate does not occur; it does not mean that the sale agreement itself cannot be established. After a house sale agreement is established and before the ownership of the house is transferred, the creditor-debtor relationship established by the parties under the agreement still exists. The plaintiff Yu Cunku's claim that the house sale agreement is invalid on the ground that the ownership has not been changed is untenable.

Article 31 of the Urban Real Estate Administration Law provides: "When real estate is transferred or mortgaged, the ownership of the house and the land use right within the scope of the land occupied by the house shall be transferred or mortgaged simultaneously." The house sold by the plaintiff Yu Cunku is a commercial apartment developed with the approval of the law, and the State permits the transfer of real estate on such land after the completion of land use right assignment procedures. Both parties to the agreement were fully aware of this situation, and therefore the agreement contained a provision that Yu Cunku would pay the land use right assignment fee and handle the procedures for the lawful transfer of this land use right. At the time the house sale agreement was signed, although Yu Cunku had not yet obtained the land use right certificate for the land occupied by the house, this was merely a matter of when it would be obtained, not a question of whether it should or could be obtained. Moreover, the facts show that only ten days after the agreement was signed, Yu Cunku obtained the certificate of allocated land use right. Although at that time Yu Cunku only had an allocated land use right for the land, this did not affect his ability to sell his private house after completing the land assignment procedures. Yu Cunku's claim that the house sale agreement is invalid on the grounds that he had not obtained the land use right when the agreement was signed and that the land was obtained through allocation and cannot be transferred is also untenable.

In summary, the house sale agreement signed by the plaintiff Yu Cunku and the defendants Dong Chengbin and Dong Chengzhen was legally established. Article 85 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Implementation of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China (for Trial Implementation) provides: "After the lawful transfer of ownership of property, if one party reneges, it shall not be supported. If ownership of the property has not been transferred in accordance with the original agreement and one party reneges without justified reason, and the agreement can still be performed, it shall continue to be performed; if the agreement cannot be performed and causes losses to the other party, compensation liability shall be borne." Yu Cunku's reneging on various unjustified grounds after the lawful transfer of house ownership had not been completed is contrary to the principle of good faith, undermines the security of transactions, and shall not be supported. After the agreement was legally established, both parties failed to perform their mutual obligation to notify each other when moving, resulting in loss of contact and the inability to timely complete the registration procedures for the change of real estate ownership in accordance with the agreement. Both parties are at fault in this regard. The counterclaim of Dong Chengbin and Dong Chengzhen requesting that Yu Cunku be ordered to assume liability for breach of contract is also not supported. The parties shall continue to perform in accordance with the provisions of law and the agreement. Accordingly, the Guanghan City People's Court of Sichuan Province rendered the following judgment:

1. The house sale agreement signed by the plaintiff Yu Cunku and the defendants Dong Chengbin and Dong Chengzhen is legally established.

2. The plaintiff Yu Cunku shall, within 30 days after the judgment takes effect, perform the obligation of the transferor in the real estate transfer to complete the registration of transfer.

3. The land use right assignment fee for the land occupied by the transferred house shall first be advanced by the defendants Dong Chengbin and Dong Chengzhen, and then, in accordance with the agreement, the plaintiff Yu Cunku shall pay the two defendants the full amount in a lump sum within 10 days based on valid receipts. Other expenses shall be borne by the two defendants.

4. The other claims of the plaintiff Yu Cunku and the defendants Dong Chengbin and Dong Chengzhen are dismissed.

The total costs of the principal action and counterclaim, including case acceptance fees and other litigation costs, amount to RMB 9,160, of which the plaintiff Yu Cunku shall bear RMB 8,000, and the defendants Dong Chengbin and Dong Chengzhen shall jointly bear RMB 1,160.

Yu Cunku refused to accept the judgment of first instance and appealed to the Deyang Intermediate People's Court of Sichuan Province on the same grounds as in his original complaint. The appellees Dong Chengbin and Dong Chengzhen answered, requesting that the original judgment be affirmed.

The Deyang Intermediate People's Court of Sichuan Province held upon trial: Article 9 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation of Several Issues concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (I) provides: "In accordance with the provisions of Article 44, paragraph 2 of the Contract Law, if laws or administrative regulations provide that a contract shall undergo approval procedures, or that it shall undergo approval, registration, or other procedures before taking effect, and before the conclusion of the court debate in the first instance the parties have still not completed the approval procedures, or have still not completed the approval, registration, or other procedures, the people's court shall find that the contract has not taken effect; if laws or administrative regulations provide that a contract shall undergo registration procedures, but do not provide that it takes effect after registration, the failure of the parties to complete the registration procedures does not affect the validity of the contract, but the ownership of the subject matter of the contract and other real rights cannot be transferred." With reference to this provision, the appellant Yu Cunku had already obtained the ownership certificate and land use right certificate for the house in question separately long before he filed the action in the first instance, making him the lawful owner of the house. The house sale agreement signed by Yu Cunku, in his capacity as the lawful owner, with the appellees Dong Chengbin and Dong Chengzhen, was legally established. According to the principle of "the land follows the house," when Yu Cunku sold his house, the land use right obtained by him through allocation could also be transferred after he lawfully completed the corresponding procedures. Therefore, the grounds of Yu Cunku's appeal are untenable and should be dismissed. The original trial found the facts clearly, had sufficient evidence, correctly applied the law, rendered an appropriate judgment, and the trial procedures were lawful, and should be affirmed. Accordingly, in accordance with Article 153, paragraph 1, item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the court rendered the following judgment:

The appeal of the appellant Yu Cunku is dismissed, and the original judgment is affirmed.

The case acceptance fee for the second instance of RMB 8,660 shall be borne by the appellant Yu Cunku.
